full_judgment: 7. The learned Judge of the High Court fell into an error in taking the view that the alleged forcible entry into the huts belonging to the appellant did not constitute criminal trespass, inasmuch as this finding cannot be justified on the evidence on record. Apparently, this finding is based on consideration of the C.S.Khatian Exhibit C where-in the name of Raj Kumar Saha Chowdhury, father of Nakules war Saha Chowdhury, Vendor of the respondents appears, and the said vendor occupied the land mentioned in the registered sale-deed Exhibits A and B that he owned and possessed the disputed land by way of inheritance. The learned Judge while taking this view did not take proper consideration of the other materials namely the decree passed in Suit No. 4 of 1937 which stands in favour of Nagendra Kumar Saha Chowdhury the predecessor of the appellant and concurrent finding of the Courts below about the possession of the disputed huts in favor of the appellant.
